24 A miniature loudspeaker, initially at rest, falls vertically from a window in a high building. When
the speaker has fallen a distance of 10.0 m, it emits a very short pulse of sound of constant
frequency 256 Hz in all directions. The pulse of sound, travelling at a speed of 330 m s–1, is heard
by a person leaning out of the window.
Air resistance is negligible.
What is the frequency of the pulse of sound heard by the person?
A
246 Hz
B
249 Hz
C
267 Hz
D
313 Hz

hints: Notice the speaker is falling away from the person at the window, so the heard pulse must have lower frequency than $256 \text{ Hz}$.
First find the speed of the falling speaker after $10.0 \text{ m}$ using $v^2 = u^2 + 2gs$ with $u = 0$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Then use the receding-source Doppler equation $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s)$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and your $v_s$ to find the observed frequency.
walkthrough: Find the source speed at emission. It falls from rest through $s = 10.0 \text{ m}$ with $a = g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, so $v_s^2 = u^2 + 2gs = 0 + 2 \times 9.81 \times 10.0$.
Calculate $v_s = \sqrt{196.2} \approx 14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ downwards, directly away from the observer at the window.
Recall the Doppler effect for a moving source and stationary observer. Because the source recedes, successive wavefronts are spread out and observed wavelength increases.
Use $f_o = f_s \times v/(v+v_s)$ where $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is wave speed and $f_s = 256 \text{ Hz}$.
Round to $246 \text{ Hz}$ with a unit check in $\text{Hz}$. The frequency is lower than $256 \text{ Hz}$, as expected for recession. This is option A.

A.explanation: Receding source gives $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s) \approx 246 \text{ Hz}$, matching the lower observed frequency.

B.explanation: 249 Hz is too high and does not follow from $v_s = 14 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in the receding-source Doppler equation.

C.explanation: 267 Hz is an increased frequency for an approaching source, but the speaker is falling away from the person at the window.

D.explanation: 313 Hz is much too high and would require the source speed to be added incorrectly as if approaching at high speed.
